source_acquisition.search_note: PDF 首页、正文、参考文献和 OpenReview 页面线索均先核查；OpenReview API 在本次检索返回 challenge verification，故以本地官方 proceedings PDF 为 Figure/Table 清单事实源。按协议运行 unicli search、agent-reach doctor --json、gh auth status，并用 gh API 检查 inventory 的 neilkale/mrt-vercel-app、scaleapi/mrt 及候选 OpenHands/Needle-in-a-Haystack。reports/tables/visual_source_inventory.csv 将 neilkale/mrt-vercel-app 标为 repository_without_visual_source；其 README 只说明轨迹查看器，未提供论文绘图源。进一步的 GitHub tree 检查发现 scaleapi/mrt README 标题与论文完全匹配，且 notebooks/final 下有 awareness/lower-bound、chunk-size/µ、capability-gap 和 human-augmentation 绘图 notebook，因此将其提升为最可信的部分视觉源；截图 app 的 UI 源仍保留在 neilkale 仓库。scaleapi/mrt 的 notebook/source tree 没有 Figure 1/2 方法示意、Figure 10/11 失败分析、Figure 17/18 全部 policy slice 的独立资产、Figure 19 threat-model 插画或论文内嵌 screenshots 的原始导出文件；因此状态为 partial_visual_source，而不是 exact_visual_source。源代码给出的字体、palette、figsize、error-bar API 和导出 dpi 只在对应对象中标为 source_exact/mixed，其余数值与颜色以 200 dpi PDF 渲染估计。

paper_style.palette_strategy: 主结果稳定使用 Baseline/Sequential/Hierarchical/Hybrid 的浅蓝、浅桃、鲑色、深红四项 palette，并用透明度叠加区分 unaware/aware 或 no-strategy/lower-bound；capability scatter 复用方法颜色，chunk/ensemble heatmap 使用 coolwarm，human feedback 使用蓝橙绿红，UI screenshot 使用深海军蓝界面。颜色通常与方法名、alpha、hatch、矩阵位置或直接数值冗余，但复杂小图灰度可读性有限。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF 正文、caption、表格和大量主结果线条为矢量；Figure 8 p.8 的四个小图、Figure 7/9 的热图色带、Figure 19 的图标、Figure 20 的工作流/分布图以及 Figures 21–23 明确含嵌入 raster image objects，故全篇为 mixed vector/raster。所有 56 页先以 200 dpi 渲染；含对象的 p.2、p.5、p.7–9、p.16–19、p.21–26、p.36、p.40、p.50、p.55–56 逐对象检查，其余正文、参考文献和附录页面逐页核对版面与清单。
paper_style.style_consistency: ICLR 2026 双栏主文与附录保持 Nimbus Roman/LinLibertine 文字、booktabs 表格和 caption 位置的一致外壳；图内定量标签主要采用 Linux Libertine O/LinLibertine 风格，来源 notebook 的字号在最终嵌入后缩小。概念图、UI screenshot 与论文文字混用 Arial/Inter、Type3 Libertine 和 raster 字样，结构和颜色复用强于字体完全一致。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: The main contributions of this work include (A) a novel computer-use sabotage benchmark, (B) analysis of red-teaming strategies for agent monitors, and (C) an agent monitoring setup that remains powerful when the monitor model has weaker capabilities than the attacker.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel A uses blue environment boxes and red/pink task boxes; panel B uses neutral robot/cartoon drawings and strategy labels; panel C uses gray Baseline versus red Our Method with dashed trend lines.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: within panel C and local labels

encodings.x: Panel C: weak-to-strong attacker capability from weak to strong
encodings.color: environment/task components in A; strategy labels in B; Baseline versus Our Method in C
encodings.shape: rounded boxes, agent/monitor icons, tool icons, and illustrative points
encodings.line: arrows connect main/side tasks, attacker tools and monitor; dashed trends in C
encodings.facet: (A) SHADE-Arena/CUA-SHADE-Arena environments; (B) monitor hijacking, lying, CoT obfuscation; (C) weak-to-strong scaling
encodings.text: Main Task, Side Task, SHADE-Arena, CUA-SHADE-Arena, strategy labels, Weak/Strong Attacker/Monitor, Monitoring AUC

figures.data_and_statistics: Composite overview rather than an estimator: A defines main/side tasks and attacker/monitor interfaces, B names three evasion policies, and C gives an illustrative two-curve weak-to-strong trend without numeric tick values or error bars.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction motivates covert misbehavior and monitoring limits → Figure 1 packages the benchmark, red-team strategy family and weak-to-strong claim → Figure 2 gives the monitor scaffold interface → Figures 3–5 test the resulting comparisons.
design_strengths: Three contributions are separated into lettered panels with a left-to-right reading order.
The same task, agent, monitor and strategy concepts used in the methods are visible before the quantitative results.
Arrows, boxes and labels provide shape/text redundancy for a conceptual object.
design_weaknesses: The overview mixes a detailed environment schematic, cartoon strategy vignettes and a qualitative scaling plot with different visual grammars.
Panel C has no numeric data or uncertainty, so the headline trend cannot be audited from this figure alone.
Many small labels and icon raster objects become difficult to read at page-width reduction; color is not robust to grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a three-panel overview that first defines the evaluation interface, then names adversarial strategies, then previews the central capability-gap claim; keep each panel’s grammar distinct and explicitly mark illustrative trends.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Baseline monitoring (blue) can be improved by splitting the trajectory into smaller chunks. These chunks can be evaluated in order (light red) or in parallel (medium red). The two techniques can be combined via a weighted average (dark red).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue denotes the full-trajectory Baseline; light red denotes Sequential chunks; medium red denotes Hierarchical parallel chunks; dark red denotes their Hybrid weighted average; gray/black are arrows and summaries.

encodings.x: left-to-right processing stages within each scaffolding
encodings.shape: trajectory/chunk/summary boxes and monitor icons
encodings.line: arrows show data flow; vertical stacks show parallel chunks
encodings.text: Trajectory, Summary, Monitor, µ and strategy names

figures.data_and_statistics: Method diagram with no numerical sample, uncertainty or measured axis. Baseline sends the full trajectory to one monitor; Sequential carries a prior summary through chunks; Hierarchical summarizes chunk scores in parallel and recursively; Hybrid combines the two scores with µ.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.5 defines the four scaffolds and inline hybrid relation → Figure 2 is the method-interface object → Figure 3/4 compare their reliability and Figure 7–9 ablate chunks, weights and same-family ensembles.
design_strengths: Four columns make the comparison a single scan rather than four prose definitions.
Color plus explicit arrows and labels distinguish parallel aggregation from sequential state passing.
The hybrid column exposes the tunable µ interface used later in Appendix D.
design_weaknesses: Dense arrows and repeated “Monitor/Summary” boxes create a high local visual load.
The caption defines color tones but does not spell out what each recursive aggregation stage receives or returns.
The diagram is a method abstraction; it does not show token counts, latency or an example trajectory.
figures.reusable_pattern: Compare baseline, sequential, hierarchical and hybrid as parallel pipeline columns, with the aggregation direction and weighted interface visible in the same frame.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Monitor (Claude 3.6 Sonnet) AUC (top) and TPR at FPR = 0.01 (bottom) against attackers in SHADE-Arena and CUA-SHADE-Arena. The light bar shows the AUC against an unaware attacker, the medium bar shows the reduced AUC against a simple aware attacker with no strategies.

color.semantic_mapping: Baseline, Sequential, Hierarchical, Hybrid are ordered light blue, light peach, salmon, and dark red; alpha/dark overlays distinguish attacker condition or lower bound.

encodings.x: Monitor Awareness: Unaware, Aware, Omniscient
encodings.y: AUC (top row) and TPR at FPR = 0.01 (bottom row)
encodings.shape: grouped bars; light/medium alpha overlay identifies unaware versus simple aware attacker
encodings.facet: (a) Claude 3.6 Sonnet/SHADE-Arena; (b) Gemini 2.5 Pro Thinking/SHADE-Arena; (c) Claude Sonnet 4 OpenHands/CUA-SHADE-Arena; metric rows
encodings.text: AUC, TPR at FPR=0.01, model/dataset subcaptions and Monitor Awareness ticks

figures.data_and_statistics: Six grouped-bar panels show trajectory-level AUC and threshold TPR for three attacker/environment settings, four scaffoldings and three monitor-awareness levels. Light bars represent unaware attackers and medium-alpha bars simple aware attackers with no explicit strategy; error bars are visible but their statistic is not defined in the caption.
figures.evidence_relation: Q1/Q3 and Findings 1–3 ask whether agent awareness dominates monitor awareness → Figure 3 is the first aggregate comparison → Figure 4 changes the aware-agent condition to worst-case strategy aggregation → Figure 5 tests capability gaps.
design_strengths: Common axes, bar order and colors support comparisons across all three agent/environment settings.
Rows separate ranking performance from the fixed-FPR operating point.
Opacity makes the unaware-versus-aware attacker contrast visible without doubling the number of bar positions.
design_weaknesses: Six small panels and four bars per group leave limited room for readable tick labels and error-bar caps.
The caption only explicitly defines bar opacity for AUC even though the lower row uses the same visual treatment; error-bar type and denominator are unspecified.
Color and alpha carry several meanings simultaneously, which is fragile under grayscale and low-resolution reproduction.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use repeated two-row grouped bars with a stable scaffold palette and a light/medium condition overlay; keep model/environment as column facets and metric as row facets.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Monitor (Claude 3.6 Sonnet) AUC (top) and TPR at FPR = 0.01 (bottom) against aware attackers in SHADE-Arena and CUA-SHADE-Arena. Medium bars show performance against attackers with no strategy, dark bars show the empirical lower bound across all non-baseline strategies.

color.semantic_mapping: Baseline, Sequential, Hierarchical, Hybrid are ordered light blue, light peach, salmon, and dark red; alpha/dark overlays distinguish attacker condition or lower bound.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: above local plots; mini tables at right

encodings.x: Monitor Awareness: Unaware, Aware, Omniscient
encodings.color: four scaffoldings; medium bars no-strategy, dark bars empirical lower bound
encodings.shape: overlaid grouped bars plus two compact Winning Scaffolding tables
encodings.facet: SHADE-Arena upper band and CUA-SHADE-Arena lower band; AUC/TPR rows
encodings.text: dataset labels, winning scaffold and exact AUC/TPR operating values

figures.data_and_statistics: Four bar panels (two datasets × two metrics) compare no-strategy medium bars with the minimum over all non-baseline strategies in dark bars. The two right-side mini tables list the winning scaffold and value for each monitor-awareness level: SHADE AUC Hybrid 0.75/0.73/0.80 and TPR Baseline 0.20/Hybrid 0.21/Baseline 0.47; CUA AUC Hybrid 0.85/0.84/0.98 and TPR Hybrid 0.68/0.67/0.88. Error-bar type remains unspecified.
figures.evidence_relation: Findings 4–6 state that evasion harms baseline and hybrid is most robust → Figure 4 gives the worst-case aggregation used for that claim → Figures 17–18 provide each policy slice and Figure 14–15 reproduce the comparison on BashBench.
design_strengths: The dark-versus-medium contrast makes the adversarial lower-bound operation legible.
Embedded winning-scaffold tables preserve exact values beside dense plots.
Dataset bands and metric rows establish a consistent reading direction.
design_weaknesses: The figure is overloaded: six plot/table regions, repeated legends and multiple alpha encodings make quick comparison difficult.
A minimum over heterogeneous attack strategies is an aggregate endpoint; the caption does not state each strategy or sample count.
Mini tables use small text and duplicate the plot’s color semantics without a clear key for the lower-bound construction.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair an empirical lower-bound overlay with a small exact winner table, but define the aggregation operator and uncertainty in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Monitor AUC against aware attackers with partial verbalization in SHADE-Arena, plotted against three measures of the attacker–monitor capability gap: (a) MMLU-Pro, (b) HELM Capabilities, and (c) SWE-Bench Verified.

color.semantic_mapping: Four monitor scaffoldings use the same palette across capability axes; color is repeated in the legend and trendline.

encodings.x: attacker capability score − monitor capability score for MMLU-Pro, HELM Capabilities, and SWE-Bench Verified
encodings.shape: square points for attacker–monitor pairs
encodings.text: metric names, AUC ticks, four scaffold labels

figures.data_and_statistics: Three linear scatter panels show AUC for aware attackers with partial verbalization across attacker–monitor pairs. The x-axis is a capability gap, y is trajectory-level AUC, and dashed lines are fitted per-scaffold trends; no confidence band, point-level uncertainty, correlation coefficient or p-value is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Q4 asks whether weak monitors can oversee stronger agents → Figure 5 is the main capability-gap evidence → Figures 12–13 separate absolute monitor and attacker capability, while Figure 16 reproduces the gap view on BashBench.
design_strengths: The same x/y definitions across three benchmark capability scores support triangulation.
Square points and color-consistent trend lines make the four scaffolds easy to track.
A page-width layout gives enough horizontal space for the long metric labels.
design_weaknesses: Each panel has different x ranges, so vertical or slope comparisons across measures are not direct.
Trend lines imply a relationship but the caption omits fitting method, sample count and uncertainty.
Four colors with similar warm tones are difficult to distinguish in dense regions and in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned capability-gap scatter facets with identical scaffold colors and per-series fitted lines, and pair the visual trend with a coefficient/uncertainty table elsewhere.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Effect of different feedback strategies on suspiciousness ratings for attacker (solid) and benign (hatched) trajectories. We compare four strategies: baseline with no annotations (blue), human feedback (orange), human feedback with a strong prior (green), and strong prior with selective escalation (red). Workflow details and screenshots are in Appendix Q.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/orange/green/red identify no annotations, raw human feedback, strong prior, and strong-prior selective escalation; hatch distinguishes benign distributions.

encodings.x: four human-feedback strategies
encodings.y: suspiciousness value (left) and TPR at FPR=0.01 (right)
encodings.shape: solid malicious versus hatched benign violins; bars on right
encodings.text: AUC labels above violin pairs and mean± value labels above TPR bars

figures.data_and_statistics: Left panel overlays malicious solid and benign hatched suspiciousness distributions for four policies; each pair is annotated with AUC 0.744, 0.727, 0.764 and 0.749. Right panel reports TPR 0.210±0.064, 0.049±0.062, 0.294±0.087 and 0.360±0.056 at FPR=0.01. The paper states three human annotations are aggregated by median, but does not define the ± statistic.
figures.evidence_relation: Q5/human-in-the-loop extension → Figure 6 connects a workflow policy to score distributions and the fixed-FPR operating point → Figure 20 expands the workflow and repeats these outcome plots → screenshots Figure 21–23 show the review interface.
design_strengths: Solid/hatch is a strong non-color distinction between malicious and benign distributions.
AUC annotations bridge the distribution panel to ranking performance, while the bar panel shows the operational threshold metric.
The four policies are kept in the same order and color across both panels.
design_weaknesses: Long policy labels and paired distributions are cramped at single-column width.
The ± values and error bars lack a named uncertainty statistic and denominator; the caption does not specify the A–A threat model or 60-minute session.
The plots mix individual points, density geometry and bars without describing smoothing or point sampling choices.
figures.reusable_pattern: Present human escalation as paired distribution and threshold-performance panels, using hatch for class and exact values as direct labels.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Monitor AUC and TPR at FPR=0.01 for the hierarchical, sequential, and hybrid (µ = 0.5) monitor, plotted against the chunk size.

color.semantic_mapping: Coolwarm cells encode AUC or TPR magnitude; numbers and colorbars repeat the quantitative mapping.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: above line panel; colorbars on heatmaps

encodings.x: chunk size 3–9 for the line panel; sequential chunk size on heatmap columns
encodings.y: AUC/TPR at FPR=0.01; hierarchical chunk size on heatmap rows
encodings.shape: circle markers on line curves; annotated square cells
encodings.line: solid scaffold curves and dashed Baseline reference
encodings.facet: AUC versus chunk size; hybrid AUC heatmap; hybrid TPR heatmap
encodings.text: cell values, axis labels, colorbars and µ=0.5 annotation

figures.data_and_statistics: A three-part ablation: left line plot compares Hierarchical, Sequential, Hybrid and dashed Baseline over chunk size; middle and right heatmaps enumerate hybrid AUC and TPR across 7×7 hierarchical/sequential chunk-size pairs. Main text reports the AUC maximum at sequential size 6 and hierarchical size 4, while the main setting is 5/5 and µ=0.5. No uncertainty is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: §3.5 defines chunking and hybrid score → Figure 7 tests chunk-size sensitivity and supplies the 6/4 operating-point evidence → Figure 8 varies µ and Figure 9 tests same-family ensembles.
design_strengths: Line and heatmap views expose both one-dimensional trends and joint chunk interactions.
Cell annotations make the grid numerically inspectable and colorbars define magnitude.
The main setting (µ=0.5) is held fixed in the joint heatmaps, matching the methods description.
design_weaknesses: Heatmaps use many tiny numbers and narrow color strips; values are hard to read when reduced.
The caption does not say which heatmap row/column is fixed or define error handling.
The line plot and heatmaps use different grammars and only partially shared encodings, so the visual relation requires prose.
figures.reusable_pattern: Combine a one-dimensional chunk sweep with a joint heatmap for the two chunk parameters, annotate cells, and mark the chosen operating point in the surrounding text.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Monitor AUC for various hybrid monitors, plotted against µ such that hybrid_suspicious_score = µ * sequential_suspicious_score + (1 − µ) * hierarchical_suspicious_score. µ = 1 corresponds to sequential monitoring, and µ = 0 corresponds to hierarchical monitoring.

color.semantic_mapping: Each colored line is an equal sequential/hierarchical chunk-size pair S=H=3,…,9; line label gives the pair and y is AUC.

encodings.x: hybrid weight µ from 0 to 1
encodings.shape: circular markers at sampled µ values
encodings.text: µ endpoints and Chunk Sizes legend

figures.data_and_statistics: One linear panel sweeps µ for seven equal chunk-size pairs. The caption and x-axis establish µ=1 as Sequential and µ=0 as Hierarchical; curves are point estimates without bands or error bars.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 7 identifies chunk sensitivity → Figure 8 tests the hybrid mixing definition and motivates the paper’s fixed µ=0.5 choice → Figure 9 checks whether gains are merely same-family ensembling.
design_strengths: The endpoint semantics make the hybrid interpolation immediately interpretable.
Seven pair labels preserve the interaction between weighting and chunk size.
Markers and lines provide a redundant path through the µ sweep.
design_weaknesses: Seven similarly colored lines and an external legend are dense for a single-column plot.
The caption does not state the number of trajectories or uncertainty computation.
No vertical line marks µ=0.5, the chosen value, so the design decision is not directly visible.
figures.reusable_pattern: Plot a tunable mixture on a shared 0–1 axis with endpoint semantics and a compact series label that includes the paired hyperparameters.

evidence.label: p.17 Figure 8 full object, labels, caption, and surrounding layout inspected from 200 dpi render

figures.label: Figure 9

caption.text: Monitor AUC for ensembles (µ = 0.5) of two hierarchical (left) or two sequential (right) monitors, plotted against the chunk size.

color.semantic_mapping: Coolwarm cells encode AUC or TPR magnitude; numbers and colorbars repeat the quantitative mapping.

encodings.x: second monitor chunk size 3–9
encodings.shape: 7×7 square cells with numeric annotation
encodings.text: AUC values in every cell, separate colorbars and family titles

figures.data_and_statistics: Two 7×7 annotated AUC matrices for µ=0.5 ensembles of two hierarchical or two sequential monitors. Each cell is an AUC point estimate for a pair of chunk sizes; no uncertainty, ensemble diversity measure or baseline reference is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: The authors use Figure 9 to test whether hybrid gains are only variance/coverage gains from ensembling → it follows Figure 7–8 chunk/µ ablations and supports the interpretation of hybrid as cross-family combination.
design_strengths: Side-by-side matrices make the same-family comparison direct.
Every cell carries a value, avoiding reliance on color alone.
Square cells and identical chunk-size domains support visual alignment.
design_weaknesses: The two panels have independent colorbars/limits that may hide cross-panel magnitude differences.
The caption omits which axis corresponds to which monitor and how the two monitors are selected.
Dense annotations and narrow colorbars are difficult to read at normal paper scale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned annotated matrices for pairwise hyperparameter sweeps, with identical axes and explicit panel-specific colorbars.

figures.label: Figure 10

caption.text: Sequential monitoring achieves higher AUC than hierarchical monitoring on shorter trajectories, while hierarchical outperforms sequential on trajectories over 60 messages (left). Sequential and baseline monitoring perform markedly better on easier tasks, with higher main task success rates (right) (Claude 3.6 attacker, Claude 3.6 monitor).

color.semantic_mapping: The linked notebooks use a four-entry coolwarm palette for Baseline, Sequential, Hierarchical, Hybrid; the hex values here are rendered approximations.

encodings.x: trajectory length bins (left) or main-task success rate (right)
encodings.shape: lines/markers for length bins and scatter points by monitor
encodings.line: solid series curves; no fitted reference line
encodings.text: n=75, 356, 125, 68, 32 under trajectory bins; legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Left panel compares AUC by five assistant-message bins with sample sizes shown below ticks: 0–20 (75), 20–40 (356), 40–60 (125), 60–80 (68), 80–100 (32). Right panel relates AUC to main-task success rate for four scaffolds. No error bars or regression uncertainty is visible.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix E asks why sequential and hierarchical fail differently → Figure 10 supplies length and task-difficulty stratification → Figure 11 drills down to task-level differences and qualitative transcript examples.
design_strengths: The two panels turn a vague architecture comparison into interpretable length and difficulty axes.
Sample counts are printed under the bins, making sparse tail bins visible.
The common scaffold palette connects both panels to the main results.
design_weaknesses: The right panel’s task-level observations are not clearly linked to point labels, and no fit or uncertainty is supplied.
The left panel connects bins but does not state whether lines are merely visual joins or estimates.
Long bin labels and small legend compete for space.
figures.reusable_pattern: Stratify aggregate monitor performance by trajectory length and task success before making mechanism claims, and show denominators under bins.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: The AUC difference between sequential and hierarchical monitoring varies across tasks (left). The sequential monitor often has higher suspicion of malicious trajectories (right).

color.semantic_mapping: Left bars use red Hierarchical Better, blue Sequential Better and gray Neither; right points use a blue–red colorbar for AUC(Hierarchical−Sequential), with x/y suspicion differences.

encodings.y: AUC difference Hierarchical−Sequential (left) or benign suspicion difference (right)
encodings.color: better-monitor category on left; AUC difference on right
encodings.shape: bars with error bars; task points with selected direct labels
encodings.facet: task-wise AUC difference and suspicion-difference scatter
encodings.text: task names, category legend, selected task labels and diverging colorbar

figures.data_and_statistics: Left panel orders many tasks by AUC(Hierarchical−Sequential), with error bars and three category colors; right panel plots attacker versus benign suspicion differences, adds zero guides and labels selected tasks, and colors points by the same AUC difference. No test or interval definition accompanies the error bars.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 10’s length/success stratification → Figure 11 identifies task-specific mechanism and false-positive tradeoffs → transcript examples below explain why flight-booking and networking tasks reverse the aggregate ordering.
design_strengths: Task ordering and zero guides make direction of monitor advantage easy to scan.
The linked bar/scatter views separate ranking outcome from malicious/benign suspicion mechanisms.
Direct labels on representative outliers connect the plot to the prose examples.
design_weaknesses: Rotated task labels are tiny and numerous; bars with overlapping error bars are hard to compare.
The right colorbar and x/y differences require careful sign interpretation; caption does not define the exact subtraction direction.
No sample counts or uncertainty estimator are given, so task-level differences may be over-read.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a sorted difference bar panel plus a mechanism scatter with zero guides and selective direct labels, and state both subtraction direction and denominator.

figures.label: Figure 12

caption.text: Monitor AUC against aware attackers with partial verbalization in SHADE-Arena, plotted against three measures of the monitor capability: (a) MMLU-Pro, (b) HELM Capabilities, and (c) SWE-Bench Verified.

color.semantic_mapping: Four monitor scaffoldings use the same palette across capability axes; color is repeated in the legend and trendline.

encodings.x: absolute monitor capability score (MMLU-Pro, HELM Capabilities, SWE-Bench Verified)
encodings.shape: square capability-pair points
encodings.text: capability metric labels and monitor legend

figures.data_and_statistics: Three scatter panels hold the aware-agent/partial-verbalization SHADE setting and place AUC against absolute monitor capability. Points are grouped by scaffold and fit with dashed trends; no confidence bands, counts, coefficients or p-values are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 5’s gap can combine attacker and monitor variation → Figure 12 isolates monitor capability → Figure 13 isolates attacker capability → the pair supports the paper’s claim that the monitor side drives more of the weak-to-strong trend.
design_strengths: The three capability measures repeat the same grammar, making directionality easy to compare.
Absolute monitor capability is separated from the gap variable, clarifying one possible mechanism.
Trend lines use the same method palette as the main figures.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not state the fitting method or which attacker/monitor pairs are included.
Different x scales and point densities across panels limit direct slope comparison.
Color-only series identity remains fragile in grayscale and in overlapping points.
figures.reusable_pattern: Decompose a capability-gap claim into aligned absolute-monitor and absolute-attacker scatter facets with the same point-level unit.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 在引言中先定义两个环境、三类规避策略和弱到强预期；Figure 2 将 baseline/sequential/hierarchical/hybrid 变成可比较的方法接口。Figure 3 先分离 agent 与 monitor awareness，Figure 4 再将策略集合压缩为 worst-case lower bound，Figure 5 用 capability-gap scatter 收束主张。附录 Figure 6 接入 human-in-the-loop，Figures 7–9 消融 chunk/µ/ensemble，Figures 10–13 分解长度、任务差异和 capability，Figures 14–18 做 BashBench 与 policy-slice 复核，Figure 19 固化 threat-model 矩阵，Figure 20–23 把人工审计流程落到 UI。Tables 1–3 分别补成本、攻击策略分布和 CUA 任务宇宙。
cross_object_system.caption_system: Caption 统一采用 Figure/Table 标签加动作句；主结果 caption 说明模型、数据集、指标和颜色/alpha 语义，附录 caption 说明复制、消融或工作流。Figure 10/11 在 caption 中直接陈述方向性发现，Figure 17/18 则把 policy 语义留给小面板标题。多数图注不说明 run count、error-bar/± 的统计类型、拟合方法或分母；截图图注仅命名 UI 内容。
cross_object_system.table_header_system: 三张表均为单层表头但职责不同：Table 1 用 Monitor Strategy/Input/Output/Cost/Latency 形成资源决策面；Table 2 用 Strategy/Description/Count/% Caught 形成攻击策略 taxonomy；Table 3 用 Main Task/Side Task 固化 CUA paired-task universe。booktabs 或 partial horizontal rules 取代竖线，只有 Table 1/2 的模型组或自然段描述承担层级。
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 的四列接口对应 Figures 3–4 的 scaffold bar comparisons；Figure 4 lower-bound panel 对接 Figures 17–18 的 policy slices；Figure 5/12/13/16 将 capability-gap claim 分解与复现；Figure 7–9 将 hybrid 定义落实为 chunk/µ/ensemble ablations；Figure 6/20 将人类 feedback policy 连接到 TPR。
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: 主文 Figure 3/4 的 awareness、evasion 和 lower-bound 结果分别回指 Appendix Figures 14/15 与 17/18；Figure 5 的 gap trend 在 Figures 12/13/16 进一步拆解和复现；Figure 6 直接指向 Appendix Q 的 Figure 20 与 Figures 21–23；Table 3 规定 CUA 任务对，Figures 3/4/18 和截图用同一环境边界。
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: 正文与表格 PDF object 的 Nimbus Roman/LinLibertine、Computer Modern math、Nimbus Mono 稳定；绘图 notebook 明确设置 Linux Libertine O，但图内字号经过嵌入缩放后约 4.5–9 pt。概念图和 UI screenshot 的 Arial/Inter/raster 字样是可见例外，因而版式和颜色复用明显强于字体统一。
cross_object_system.color_consistency: 四种 monitor scaffolding 在 Figures 2–5、10、12–18 中保持浅蓝/浅桃/鲑色/深红顺序；opacity 负责 attacker condition 或 lower bound，hatch 负责 human feedback 的 benign 类别，heatmap 使用 coolwarm，UI 使用独立深色主题。方法颜色具有图例和文本冗余，但 capability scatter 与六-panel bar figure 的色相相近，灰度下仍有辨识风险。

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 2 的四列 scaffold pipeline 将信息流差异先变成可视接口，再用 Figure 3/4 的同序 bar grammar 验证主比较和 worst-case lower bound。
以 agent awareness × monitor awareness 的 2×3 threat-model 矩阵（Figure 19）预先固定信息边界，再把同一词汇复用到主结果和 BashBench 复核。
把 capability-gap 结论拆成 gap、absolute monitor 和 absolute attacker 三组同构 scatter（Figures 5、12、13、16），避免单一相关图承担全部解释。
用 Figure 6/20 的 workflow + suspiciousness distribution + TPR 组合把人工 intervention 连接到可观测结果，并用 Figures 21–23 补足具体审计界面。
将高密度 heatmap/策略表与直接数值标注配对，同时保留 Table 1–3 作为成本、攻击 taxonomy 和任务 universe 的精确承载。
highest_value_objects: Figure 4：四种 scaffold、两数据集、两指标和经验 lower bound 的核心决策图，右侧 winner tables 保留精确值。
Figure 5：主文 weak-to-strong capability-gap 证据，三种能力量度和四条 scaffold trend 放在同一页面。
Figure 2：方法接口最清晰，直接解释 sequential、hierarchical、hybrid 为何是后续比较的对象。

failure_patterns: 几乎所有定量图使用 error bars 或 ±，但 PDF caption 没有稳定命名其为 SD、SE、bootstrap CI 或其它统计量；散点 trend 也没有拟合不确定性。
多 panel bar/heatmap 依赖相近色相、alpha 和 tiny legends，缩小或灰度打印时方法与条件难以区分。

Table 1 的近似 cost/latency 打印为精确小数，Table 2 的零计数用 em dash，Table 3 缺少稳定 task ID；这些设计会让复现者误判精度或难以追踪对象。
Figure 1、Figure 2、Figure 20 将多种视觉语法放在单个 composite 中，方法/流程/结果边界需要正文文字才能完全解释。
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: 论文以 awareness 与四种 monitor scaffold 为稳定视觉词汇，从 Figure 1/2 的威胁和信息流接口出发，经 Figure 3/4 的主比较与 lower bound、Figure 5 的 capability-gap，再由附录消融、失败分解、跨 benchmark 复核和 human-review UI 完成证据闭环。
